title: Full-Stack Feature Scaffolder
description: Generates a complete full-stack boilerplate including database schema, API routes, and frontend components for a given feature.
prompt_text: Act as a senior full-stack architect. I need to build a feature for [insert feature description, e.g., 'a real-time comment section']. Provide a complete implementation plan. Output the SQL schema for PostgreSQL, the REST API endpoints using Node.js and Express with proper error handling, and the React component using hooks and a modern CSS-in-JS approach. Ensure the code handles loading and empty states. Use TypeScript strictly.

title: Legacy Code Modernizer & Documenter
description: Refactors an old, uncommented script into a clean, modular, and well-documented modern version with unit tests.
prompt_text: Analyze the following legacy code. Refactor it into a modern [insert language, e.g., Python 3.11] application using best practices (SOLID principles). Break the monolithic script into logical, reusable modules. Add comprehensive type hints and Google-style docstrings. Finally, write a full unit test suite using [insert testing framework, e.g., Pytest] to cover all edge cases, including null inputs and network timeouts. Code: [paste your legacy code here]

title: Regex Generator & Explainer
description: Creates a complex regular expression based on natural language requirements and explains every component step-by-step.
prompt_text: Generate a regular expression that matches the following pattern: [insert pattern, e.g., 'valid IPv6 addresses']. The regex must be compatible with the [insert language, e.g., JavaScript] engine. After providing the final pattern string, break down the regex into a table format. Each row should represent a distinct token/group, explaining its function and providing a specific example match for that segment. Include common pitfalls where the regex might fail.

title: Smart Code Review & Security Audit
description: Acts as a senior security-focused dev to review a pull request for logic flaws, OWASP vulnerabilities, and performance bottlenecks.
prompt_text: You are a principal engineer conducting a hardcore code review. Review the following code snippet for [insert language]. Provide feedback categorized into three buckets: 1) Critical (Security vulnerabilities like SQL injection or broken access control), 2) High (Logic errors that break core functionality), and 3) Medium (Performance improvements and code smells). Do not comment on stylistic preferences unless they significantly harm readability. For every issue, provide a concrete code suggestion fix. Code: [paste PR diff or code block]

title: System Design Trade-Off Analyzer
description: Simulates a system design interview where the AI challenges your design decisions and calculates back-of-the-envelope capacity.
prompt_text: I am designing [insert system, e.g., 'a URL shortener like Bitly']. Act as an interviewer. First, ask me clarifying questions one by one about traffic, storage, and consistency requirements. After I provide the constraints, propose a high-level architecture. Then, aggressively cross-question my choices regarding SQL vs NoSQL, caching strategies, and message queues. Conclude with a calculation of bandwidth and storage estimates for [insert scale, e.g., 100 million daily active users].

title: Psychographic Hook Generator
description: Generates 10 viral social media hooks targeting specific pain points and deep-seated desires of a niche avatar.
prompt_text: Act as a world-class direct response copywriter. I am targeting [insert target audience, e.g., 'burnt-out middle managers who want to start a side hustle']. Generate 10 distinct opening hooks for a [insert platform, e.g., LinkedIn or TikTok] post. The hooks must fall into these categories: Shocking Statistic, Contrarian View, Emotional Story, Quick Win Promise, and 'The Big Lie.' Use advanced psychological triggers like FOMO and validation. Do not write the full post, only the hooks.

title: Viral Thread Blueprint
description: Outlines a long-form educational text thread with strong cliffhangers and a high converting CTA at the end.
prompt_text: Create a viral content thread strategy on [insert topic, e.g., 'how to use ChatGPT for data analysis'] for X/Twitter. Outline a 10-tweet thread. Tweet 1: A disruptive hook. Tweets 2-8: Step-by-step actionable insights, each ending with a 'but wait...' style suspense to force the reader to unfold the thread. Tweet 9: The reveal or big 'aha' moment. Tweet 10: A soft CTA to sign up for my [insert lead magnet]. Ensure every tweet is a self-contained soundbite.

title: Multi-Platform Content Repurposer
description: Turns a single long-form video transcript into tailored posts for Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter, and TikTok with distinct tones.
prompt_text: Repurpose the following transcript into a cohesive cross-platform campaign. 1) LinkedIn: A professional story-telling post with bulleted business takeaways. 2) Instagram: A conversational, emoji-rich caption with relevant hashtags. 3) X/Twitter: A punchy thread boiling the concept down to its most controversial element. 4) TikTok/Reels: A short, fast-paced script with visual jump-cut cues and a strong text hook overlay. Transcript: [paste transcript here]

title: Ad Creative A/B Test Generator
description: Generates two distinct sets of primary text and headlines for a platform ad, split by angle (benefit-driven vs. pain-driven).
prompt_text: Generate two distinct Facebook/Instagram Ad creative variants for [insert product/service]. Variant A: 'Pain Awareness' angle focusing on the nightmare of not using the product (agitate the problem). Variant B: 'Aspirational Transformation' angle focusing on the dream outcome. For each variant, provide the Primary Text (truncated to 125 chars), the Headline (40 chars), and a visual direction prompt describing what the image/video should show. Target audience: [insert audience].

title: Trenjacking Content Brief
description: Creates a reactive content brief linking a current viral news trend to a brand’s niche without being cringey.
prompt_text: A current trending topic in pop culture/tech is [insert trend]. My business is in [insert niche, e.g., 'cybersecurity']. Create a reactive marketing brief that connects this trend to my niche naturally. Provide 3 angles: 1) The 'What can we learn' angle, 2) The 'Hot take' angle, and 3) The 'Funny observation' angle. For each, explain why the algorithm will push this content and ensure the pivot to our product doesn't feel like a sales pitch.

title: PASO Framework Pain-Point Expander
description: Writes a brutally honest landing page section using the Problem-Agitation-Solution-Outcome framework with sensory words.
prompt_text: Write a landing page 'Hero & Problem' section for [insert product/service] targeting [insert audience]. Follow the P.A.S.O framework strictly: 1. Problem: Identify the hidden root cause of their frustration. 2. Agitation: Describe the visceral, day-to-day emotional toll using sensory language (e.g., 'pounding headache,' 'pit in your stomach'). 3. Solution: Introduce our product as the logical bridge. 4. Outcome: Paint the 'Monday morning after' picture where the problem is solved. Tone: [insert, e.g., 'empathetic but urgent'].

title: Feature-to-Benefit Ladder Converter
description: Transforms boring product features into a ladder of higher-level emotional and philosophical benefits.
prompt_text: Convert the following list of product features into a 'Benefit Ladder.' For each feature, list: Level 1: The direct functional advantage. Level 2: The practical life improvement this allows. Level 3: The emotional payoff the user feels. Level 4: The identity shift or status gain. Features: [insert list of features]. Format as a detailed markdown table.

title: Objection-Busting FAQ Writer
description: Generates an FAQ section that preemptively dismantles skepticism using the 'Feel-Felt-Found' empathy method.
prompt_text: Generate an FAQ section for a high-ticket offer in [insert niche]. Identify the 5 most common purchasing objections (e.g., 'It's too expensive,' 'Will it work for me?'). Answer each using the 'Feel-Felt-Found' framework: Acknowledge how they feel, relate to someone who felt the same way, and explain what they found after purchasing. Make sure the tone is reassuring, data-backed, and closes the loop on doubt.

title: The 'Why You Shouldn't Buy' Reversal
description: Crafts a high-converting sales page section that disqualifies the wrong customers to build radical trust with the right ones.
prompt_text: Write a 'Who is this NOT for?' section for my sales page. The product is [insert product]. List 5 specific traits or situations that make a customer a bad fit. Be brutally honest and slightly abrasive to scare off refund-seekers. After listing the disqualifiers, pivot sharply with 'But if you are the kind of person who...' and list the ideal psychographic traits of our best customers. The goal is to create a 'this is exactly me' epiphany.

title: Multi-Persona Narrative Adaptor
description: Rewrites a single piece of content for three distinct reader personas to maximize market segmentation.
prompt_text: Take the following core content brief: [insert content brief]. Rewrite it into three distinct versions targeting: 1) 'The Skeptic' (data-driven, logical, needs proof, hates fluff). 2) 'The Dreamer' (big picture, wants inspiration, drawn to metaphors). 3) 'The Operator' (hands-on, wants step-by-step, pragmatist). Keep the core message identical, but change the vocabulary, metaphors, and pacing for each persona.

title: Midjourney Hyper-Realistic Texture Matcher
description: Generates a prompt for a hyper-realistic 8K image focusing on specific material textures and studio lighting setups.
prompt_text: A macro photography shot of [insert object, e.g., 'ancient samurai helmet'], hyper-detailed, 8k resolution. Focus on [insert texture, e.g., 'rusted iron and weathered silk']. Lighting: 3-point studio lighting with a rim light to highlight the silhouette, cinematic volumetric fog. Camera: Hasselblad H6D-100c, 120mm macro lens, f/2.8, shallow depth of field. Background: matte black void, light catching floating dust particles. --ar 3:2 --style raw --v 6.1

title: Consistent Character Sheet Architect
description: Creates a reference character sheet with multiple expressions and angles using seed and gen-ID parameters for consistency.
prompt_text: Full character reference sheet for [insert character description, e.g., 'a female cyberpunk mechanic']. Multiple angles: front view, 3/4 profile, back view showing backpack details. Include expression grid: neutral, laughing angrily, concentrated. Outfit must be identical in every frame. Consistent style: Studio Ghibli character design meets Moebius line art. Clean vector lines, solid color fills, minimal shading. White background. --ar 16:9 --style expressive --niji 6

title: Brand Style Guide Visual Synthesizer
description: Generates a cohesive brand design system image including logo mark, color palette swatches, and typography pairing.
prompt_text: A flat lay design, brand identity board for a [insert brand vibe, e.g., 'luxury organic skincare line named AURA']. Include minimalist logo mark (geometric, golden ratio), primary and secondary color swatches arranged neatly (earth tones: terracotta, sage, cream), typography pairing examples (sans-serif headline + elegant serif body), and curated lifestyle texture pieces (linen, dried botanicals, river stones). Clean composition, bright natural skylight, high-end editorial photography, white background. --ar 4:5 --v 6.1

title: Photorealistic Historical Unseen Moment
description: Depicts an unseen, candid 'behind-the-scenes' moment from history with precise period-accurate costuming and grain.
prompt_text: Candid shot of [insert historical scene, e.g., 'Nikola Tesla having coffee in his lab, reading a newspaper by the light of a plasma globe'], 1920s. Period-accurate fashion, vintage coffee cup. Naturalistic lighting, dust motes in sunbeams. Shot on a Leica M3, Kodak Portra 400 film stock, subtle film grain, chromatic aberration at the edges, soft vignette. The vibe is melancholic genius, intimate documentarian style, not posed. --ar 4:5 --style raw --v 6.1

title: Dribbble-Level UI/UX Mockup Render
description: Creates a highly aesthetic Dribbble-style shot of a mobile app screen on a device mockup with colorful abstract backgrounds.
prompt_text: Dribbble shot, UI/UX design mockup for a [insert app type, e.g., 'AI fitness tracker'] mobile app. iPhone 15 Pro mockup on a trending vector background (organic blob shapes, glassmorphism). The screen displays [insert key screen, e.g., 'a dashboard with vibrant stats and a heart rate graph']. Clean, modern, neumorphic design elements, 8pt grid system. Flowing fabric or floating 3D spheres next to the phone. Studio lighting, 4k, isometric view. --ar 3:2 --v 6.1

title: Retention-Hook Short Script
description: Writes a 60-second vertical video script that uses visual pattern interrupts and text overlays to maximize AVD.
prompt_text: Write a script for a 60-second YouTube Short/TikTok about [insert topic, e.g., 'a hidden iPhone gesture']. The first 1.5 seconds must have a visual shock (e.g., sudden zoom). Include precise timestamps. For every 3-4 second segment, describe the visual change (B-roll, text overlay, drastic angle change) to prevent cognitive habituation. Separate the script into 'Visual' and 'Audio/Voiceover' columns. The CTA must be a 'watch next' loop suggestion.

title: AI Animation Kinetic Typography Prompter
description: Generates a prompt for Runway or Pika to animate text with specific kinetic motion tracks and materials.
prompt_text: Generate an animation prompt for [insert AI video tool, e.g., Pika/Runway]. The subject is kinetic typography for the word '[insert word, e.g., VELOCITY]'. The letters should be constructed of [insert material, e.g., 'liquid mercury']. Movement: letters slam onto the screen from the left with overshoot physics, breaking apart slightly and reforming. Camera: dolly zoom push-in synchronized to the beat of a heavy drum. Style: photorealistic industrial, dark moody lighting, 24fps motion blur.

title: Faceless YouTube Channel Strategist
description: Outlines a complete script, voiceover direction, and b-roll sourcing map for a high-retention faceless documentary video.
prompt_text: Plan a 10-minute faceless YouTube documentary video on [insert topic, e.g., 'The fall of MoviePass']. 1. Script Outline: Opening loop, inciting incident, rising action, climax, lesson. 2. B-roll Direction: Describe exact stock footage searches (e.g., 'close up of credit cards burning') and motion graphics to explain complex data. 3. Audio: Note where the background music should drop out for silence (dramatic pause), and describe the voiceover pacing (slow and dramatic vs fast and info-dense).

title: Product Demo Cinematic Shot List
description: Generates a technical shot list for a high-end product commercial, specifying lighting ratios, focal lengths, and slider moves.
prompt_text: Create a shot list for a 30-second premium commercial video for [insert product, e.g., 'a luxury mechanical watch']. Style: Christopher Nolan cinematic meets Apple product video. List 10 shots: 1) Extreme macro glide over the gears, 2) Slow-motion splash/water test, 3) Close-up of the clasp with dramatic edge-lighting. For each shot, specify: Camera (Red Komodo), Lens (focal length/T-stop), Lighting setup (Key-to-fill ratio), and Camera Movement (slider speed/direction).

title: Storyboard to Motion Concept Translator
description: Converts a static storyboard frame description into a detailed text-to-video prompt focusing on motion vectors and zoom.
prompt_text: Translate this static scene into a dynamic text-to-video prompt for AI generation. Scene description: [insert scene, e.g., 'A samurai standing in rain']. Dynamic prompt instructions: Add motion vectors (e.g., 'wind blowing cherry blossoms left to right, fabric rippling organically'). Camera move (e.g., 'crash zoom into eyes'). Lighting change (e.g., 'lightning flash that illuminates the face for 4 frames'). Include negative prompt: 'no morphing, no flickering, high fidelity, 16mm film grain'.

title: Investor Pitch Narrative Shaper
description: Structures a startup pitch deck story arc around the hero’s journey, framing the company as the guide and the investor as the sage.
prompt_text: Structure my startup pitch deck script using the 'StoryBrand' or 'Hero's Journey' framework. Problem: [insert market problem]. Our Solution: [insert solution]. Frame the target customer as the Hero. Frame our company as the Guide (wise, empathetic, authoritative). Frame the competition as the Villain (root of the evil). Provide the concise headline for slides 1-10, ensuring the 'Financial Projection' slide is framed as the 'Reward/Crown' for the investor if the villain is defeated.

title: MECE Case Interview Drill
description: Acts as a McKinsey interviewer providing a market sizing question and grilling the user’s framework for MECE completeness.
prompt_text: You are a McKinsey Partner conducting a case interview. Give me a challenging, non-standard market sizing question related to [insert industry]. After I present my framework, critique it ruthlessly: point out any missing MECE branches, false assumptions, or overlapping categories. Then, walk me through a perfect, data-driven back-of-the-envelope calculation taking into account replacement rates and demographic segmentation. Do not make up the numbers; show the formula logically.

title: Fractional CFO Profitability Optimizer
description: Analyzes a P&L statement and spits out a radical cost-optimization plan targeting a 20% margin improvement.
prompt_text: Act as a fractional CFO for a [insert business type] company. Analyze the following P&L statement. Identify the 3 biggest levers to increase EBITDA margin by 20% within 6 months. Focus on unit economics, not just slashing overhead. Categorize costs into 'Scale-enabling' vs 'Status-quo' costs. Provide a step-by-step implementation plan with a risk register of what could break operationally if we cut those specific costs. P&L Data: [paste numbers]

title: Monte Carlo Risk Analysis Narrator
description: Converts complex investment risk statistics into an easy-to-understand narrative report for non-financial stakeholders.
prompt_text: We are evaluating an investment in [insert asset/venture]. Simulate a risk analysis. Explain the 'cone of uncertainty' for our cash flow projections. Assume a Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 trials. Interpret the output (you can simulate plausible outputs) and present the 90% confidence interval. Explain Value at Risk (VaR) and Conditional VaR in plain English. Conclude with a narrative recommendation: 'This is a bet on [X] with a floor of [Y],' written for a busy CEO who hates math.

title: Blue Ocean Strategy Canvas Generator
description: Creates a strategy canvas comparing competitors on key competing factors and visualizes an uncontested market space.
prompt_text: Generate a Blue Ocean Strategy Canvas for the [insert industry] industry. Identify the 5-7 core 'Factors of Competition' that the industry currently competes on (e.g., price, prestige, battery life). List our top 3 competitors and map their offering level (high/medium/low) on these factors. Then, apply the 'ERRC Grid' (Eliminate, Reduce, Raise, Create) to design a new value curve that makes the competition irrelevant. Describe the new Curve in text format ready for a chart.

title: Semantic Topical Map Architect
description: Creates a topical authority map with pillar pages and cluster content based on semantic SEO and entity relationships.
prompt_text: Build a topical map for a website about [insert broad niche, e.g., 'electric bikes']. Identify 1 main Pillar Page topic. Then, generate 15 Cluster Page topics. Cluster topics must cover: informational (how-to guides), commercial (comparisons), transactional (best lists), and news (industry updates). For each page, provide the target primary keyword phrase, the search intent (I/C/T/N), and a suggested URL slug. Structure this as an organized hierarchy.

title: Competitor Backlink Gap Exploiter
description: Identifies high-authority, easily replicable backlink opportunities your competitors have that you currently lack.
prompt_text: Analyze the backlink profile strategy (conceptually) for a new site in [insert niche]. We don't have access to live data, so act as a competitive strategist. Describe 5 specific types of 'Linkable Assets' or 'Link Bait' that work in this niche (e.g., 'Free calculator tool,' 'Industry salary survey,' 'Infographic of statistics'). For each asset, identify the exact query operators (e.g., 'intitle:[keyword] +
') to find sites that would likely link to us but are currently linking to our dead/redirected competitors.

title: Programmatic SEO Page Blueprint
description: Designs a Wordpress/Webflow CMS collection template for programmatic SEO pages using dynamic data variables.
prompt_text: Design a programmatic page template for [insert use-case, e.g., 'best restaurants in [city]']. The template must be de-duplicated and unique per city. Outline the structure: H1 (dynamic variable), H2 (variable-based subheading), automated opening paragraph (Mad Libs style with data points like population/cuisine), a dynamic comparison table, and a 'Local Tips' section. Provide the markdown layout of the template and define the required fields in the CMS database (e.g., City Name, Zip Code, Image URL).

title: Google E-E-A-T Content Grader
description: Evaluates an existing article draft against Google’s Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness guidelines.
prompt_text: Grade the following blog article on the E-E-A-T scale (1-10 for each). Article: [paste article text]. 1. Experience: Is there first-hand evidence/photos/data? 2. Expertise: Does the author list credentials or specific deep knowledge? 3. Authority: Is the author referenced elsewhere in the niche? 4. Trust: Is the contact info, date, and fact-checking citation obvious? Provide a rewritten intro paragraph for this article that shouts 'Experience' from the first sentence.

title: AI Content Update Decay Preventer
description: Refreshes a year-old blog post with new stats, current year references, and a fresh FAQ schema to combat content decay.
prompt_text: Update the following blog post from [insert old date] to today's context. Do not rewrite the whole thing. Instead: 1. Replace all outdated statistics with placeholders for [Current Year] stats (source needed). 2. Add a 'What's New in [Current Year]' section. 3. Generate a JSON-LD FAQ schema with 3 modern questions about the topic. 4. Suggest 2 new internal links to other relevant newer posts. Original Post: [paste text]

title: Neurolinguistic Product Description
description: Writes a sensory-rich product description that tricks the brain into simulating the experience of owning the product.
prompt_text: Write a product description for [insert product, e.g., 'weighted blanket']. Use neurolinguistic programming (NLP) sensory predicates: Visual (imagine the deep charcoal texture), Auditory (the silence of the beads shifting), Kinesthetic (the feeling of security pressing down). Do not just list specs. Describe the 'Sunday morning at 9am' feeling of using this. Structure: Attention Headline -> Sensory Scene -> Unique Tech Explanation (translated to benefits) -> Social Proof Implication -> CTA.

title: High-Converting Product Bundle Strategist
description: Analyzes a store catalog and recommends logical 'tripwire,' 'core,' and 'upsell' bundle offers with pricing justification.
prompt_text: I sell [insert product category]. Design a 3-tier bundling strategy: 1. The Tripwire (low cost, irresistible, breaks the ice, $9-$19 range). 2. The Core Bundle (the main solution, best value, anchors the price). 3. The Premium Bundle (includes exclusive digital content or personalized service). For each bundle, write a 3-bullet comparison table highlighting which pain points each tier solves and who it's perfect for. State the psychological principle behind the price gap (e.g., Decoy Effect).

title: Abandoned Cart Recovery Funnel
description: Drafts a 3-email abandoned cart sequence that uses urgency without lying, leveraging specific product imagery.
prompt_text: Create a 3-email abandoned cart sequence for [insert product name]. Email 1 (1 hour later): 'Did your cart just glitch?' – focused on helpful tech support, reminding them the item isn't reserved yet. Email 2 (12 hours later): Pain point reminder – focus on the problem the product solves, 'Don't let [insert pain] ruin your week.' Email 3 (24 hours later, with discount): Social proof testimonial + a modest time-sensitive discount (24h clock). Use curiosity-driven subject lines for all three.

title: Customer Review Extraction Analyzer
description: Scans a batch of raw customer reviews and extracts the exact 'voice of customer' phrases to use in ad copy.
prompt_text: Analyze the following raw customer reviews for [insert product]. Extract the 'Voice of Customer' data: 1. Top 3 unique phrases customers use to describe the product (verbatim, even if grammar is broken). 2. The 2 most common emotional benefits inferred. 3. The 2 most common technical complaints/frictions. Turn those complaints into a 'Objection Reversal' copy snippet we can put on the product page. Reviews: [paste batch of reviews]

title: Shopify SEO Collection Page Curator
description: Writes a unique, keyword-optimized collection page description and meta title that passes Google’s duplicate content check.
prompt_text: Write the SEO title tag (max 55 chars) and collection description (250 words) for a [insert platform, e.g., Shopify] category page: [insert category, e.g., 'Vintage Denim Jackets']. The description must be optimized for 'evergreen + transactional' keywords. Do not use AI fluffy marketing terms like 'elevate your style.' Write it as if an expert curator is describing the specific feel/weight/uniqueness of the inventory currently stocked. Add a H2 subheading variation at the bottom for a local search signal if relevant.

title: Pattern Interrupt Cold Email
description: Crafts a cold email that breaks the corporate script using a deeply researched, personal compliment or contrarian statement.
prompt_text: Write a cold email to [insert title, e.g., 'VP of Engineering'] at [insert company]. Subject line: no buzzwords, max 4 words, starting with a lowercase letter if effective (e.g., 'quick question...'). Opening line: A genuine, hyper-specific observation about their recent LinkedIn post/product launch, followed by a contrarian pattern interrupt (e.g., 'Most founders think X, but data shows Y'). Body: 3 bullet points max. CTA: 'Not looking for a call, just want to know your take on [insert niche question]?'

title: The 'Rackman Spin' Question Set
description: Generates a sequence of Situation, Problem, Implication, and Need-Payoff questions to run a discovery call.
prompt_text: Generate a SPIN selling question sequence for a [insert role] selling [insert product] to [insert prospect industry]. 1. Situation (2 questions, data-gathering but not lazy). 2. Problem (3 questions to uncover hidden inefficiencies they haven't articulated). 3. Implication (2 questions to make the cost of inaction feel huge and urgent). 4. Need-Payoff (2 questions that make them verbalize the value of solving the problem). Questions should be conversational, not robotic.

title: Advanced Objection Preemptor
description: Lists the top 10 brush-off objections (like 'not interested') and provides a psychological Jiu-Jitsu reversal for each.
prompt_text: I sell [insert product]. Give me a table of 10 'Brush-off Objections' (e.g., 'Send me an email,' 'We're good for now,' 'It's too expensive'). For each objection, provide 3 columns: 1. 'What they say', 2. 'What they really mean' (the subtext/fear), 3. 'The Permission-Based Reversal' (a script that validates their fear, gets permission to dig deeper, and reframes the value). Tone: consultative, non-salesy, zero pressure.

title: LinkedIn Voice Note Pitch Scripter
description: Writes a concise script for a LinkedIn voice DM that sounds spontaneous and leverages audio intimacy for connecting.
prompt_text: Write a script for a LinkedIn audio voice note DM (max 40 seconds). The goal is to schedule a discovery call regarding [insert service]. The background sound should be referenced as a human touch point (e.g., 'I'm just walking out of a client meeting...'). Structure: 1. Reason for voice note (text is too impersonal). 2. The 'I saw your [specific post/achievement]' hook. 3. The 'I struggled with similar' common enemy bonding. 4. A super soft CTA: 'If you record a reply right now, I'll listen.'

title: BANT Qualification Flowchart Logic
description: Provides a decision-tree logic for screening leads using Budget, Authority, Need, and Timeline criteria.
prompt_text: Create a decision tree logic flow for screening inbound leads for [insert high-ticket B2B service]. Map out the BANT criteria in a logical 'If/Else' script format. 1. Budget: How to subtly pivot from 'How much does it cost?' to 'What is the cost of the problem?' 2. Authority: Multi-threading questions to find the economic buyer. 3. Need: Trigger event indicators. 4. Timeline: Questions that create a compelling event. Output as a flowchart in markdown.

title: Second Brain PARA System Migrator
description: Analyzes a chaotic task dump and sorts it into the PARA (Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives) folder system.
prompt_text: Act as a knowledge management expert. Here is a brain dump of my current tasks and interests: [insert random task list]. Sort these into the PARA system for a tool like Notion or Obsidian. 1. Projects: Active, specific outcomes with deadlines. 2. Areas: Ongoing standards of responsibility. 3. Resources: Topic-based interests. 4. Archives: Completed/inactive. Output a markdown checklist with the items assigned.

title: Intelligent Daily Time-Blocker
description: Takes a list of tasks and contextual energy levels to create a chronotype-optimized daily schedule.
prompt_text: I am a [insert chronotype, e.g., 'Lion' (early bird)]. My peak focus hours are [insert hours]. Here is my to-do list: [insert tasks]. Categorize these tasks into Deep Work (high cognitive load), Admin Work (shallow), and Creative. Build a precise time-blocked schedule for tomorrow, inserting 15-min buffer blocks between them. Ensure no deep work is scheduled during my post-lunch slump. Include a 'Shutdown ritual' block at the end.

title: Meeting Agenda to Action Minutes
description: Converts a messy meeting transcript or bullet list into a structured 'Decisions, Owners, Deadlines' output.
prompt_text: Parse the following meeting notes into 'Action-First Minutes.' Do not write chronological narration. Format strictly as: 1. Key Decisions Made (with brief rationale). 2. Action Items (Table format: Task, Owner, Deadline, Dependencies). 3. Parking Lot (Topics raised but deferred). 4. Next Steps (Single sentence closing statement). Meeting Notes: [paste messy notes]

title: Process Documentation SOP Creator
description: Generates a visual-heavy, foolproof Standard Operating Procedure markdown that requires zero prior knowledge.
prompt_text: Create a crisp SOP (Standard Operating Procedure) for [insert task, e.g., 'publishing a weekly newsletter']. The document must be readable by a complete beginner. Use the checklist method for each step. Structure: Objective -> Time to Complete -> Prerequisites (tools/logins) -> The Step-by-Step (with emojis for visual scanning) -> Quality Assurance (validation checklist) -> Common Errors & Troubleshooting. Format as raw Markdown.

title: The Eisenhower Matrix Prioritizer
description: Analyzes a complex backlog of tasks, applying the Eisenhower Matrix with advanced decision criteria.
prompt_text: Analyze my current workload using the Eisenhower Matrix. However, do not just put things in Urgent/Important. Apply a 2-layer filter: 1. 'Does this create a leveraged asset?' 2. 'Will the consequences of not doing this compound negativity?' Tasks: [insert task list]. Output a 4-quadrant chart (Do, Schedule, Delegate, Delete). For 'Delegate,' specify the exact briefing I need to give. For 'Delete,' provide the 'sunk cost' reasoning to help me let go.

title: The Feynman Technique Teacher
description: Explains a highly complex topic using only the 1,000 most common English words, simple analogies, and diagrams.
prompt_text: Explain [insert complex topic, e.g., 'Quantum Entanglement'] using the Feynman Technique. Step 1: Explain the concept as if to a 12-year-old, using only the 1,000 most common English words. Step 2: Identify gaps in that simplified explanation where nuance was lost. Step 3: Fill those gaps with a 'real world' analogy involving [insert something simple, e.g., socks and drawers]. Step 4: Provide a short text-art diagram or flowchart.

title: Interleaved Practice Curriculum
description: Designs a study plan that mixes different types of problems, bypassing the fluency illusion for maximum retention.
prompt_text: Design a 4-week study plan for mastering [insert skill, e.g., 'Data Structures in Python']. Do not block practice by topic. Use Interleaving: in each daily session, mix 3 different concept types (e.g., Sorting, Trees, and Linked Lists). For each week, specify the 'mixing formula.' Add 'Desirable Difficulties' (e.g., forcing recall from memory before looking at notes). Output a grid view of the weekly plan.

title: Socratic Method Debate Bot
description: Engages the user in a Socratic dialogue, questioning their assumptions about a topic to reach deeper understanding.
prompt_text: You are a Socratic tutor. I am your student. I will give you a statement about [insert topic]. Your job is not to correct me, but to ask me a series of deep, probing questions to test the foundation of my beliefs. Start with: 'Why do you believe that is the case?' Lead me through a dialogue that uncovers contradictions and forces me to refine my definition. Do not give answers. Just ask the next question based on my response.

title: Academic Abstract Distiller
description: Condenses a dense research paper into a 5-card 'Research Haiku,' summarizing the background, method, results, and critique.
prompt_text: Summarize the following academic paper into '5 Snap Cards.' Card 1: Background (Why did they bother? - 2 sentences). Card 2: Methodology (How exactly did they test it? - 2 sentences). Card 3: Key Result (The 'Holy Cow' finding - 1 sentence). Card 4: Limitations (The 'Yeah, but...' factor mentioned by authors). Card 5: TL;DR Bottom Line (One sentence takeaway for an industry practitioner). Paper Text: [paste paper section]

title: Memory Palace Architect
description: Converts a dry list of facts into a vivid, humorous, and sensory-heavy 'memory palace' journey narrative.
prompt_text: I need to memorize a list of [insert list of items/concepts, e.g., 'the 7 base SI units']. Create a 'Memory Palace' script. Use my home as the default location, walking from the front door through the house. For each item, assign a bizarre, multi-sensory image (exaggerated, sexual, funny, or violent) placed in a specific spot. The narrative must link the images in sequence. End with a quick 'recap' walk-through.

title: Bias-Free Job Description Optimizer
description: Rewrites a job description to remove gendered language and corporate jargon while accurately mapping technical skills.
prompt_text: Rewrite the following job description for [insert role]. Apply the following filters: 1. Gender Decoder: Remove masculine-coded words (e.g., 'ninja,' 'crush,' 'dominate') and feminine-coded over-compensations. 2. Jargon Killer: Translate 'synergistic thought leadership' into plain speech. 3. Responsibility vs. Requirements: Split vague responsibilities into clear 'Day 1, Week 1, Month 1' expectations. 4. Inclusive Add-on: Add a 'non-traditional backgrounds welcome' statement that feels authentic. Original JD: [paste]

title: Competency-Based Interview Kit
description: Generates a structured interview scorecard with CARL (Context-Action-Result-Learning) questions targeting key competencies.
prompt_text: I'm hiring a senior [insert role] for a [insert company stage, e.g., fast-paced Series B startup]. The 3 core competencies needed are: [insert 3 soft skills, e.g., 'Resilience,' 'Strategic Thinking,' 'Collaboration']. Generate 3 behavioral interview questions per competency using the CARL framework. For the interviewer script, include 'Probing Follow-ups' (e.g., 'What did you specifically say in that meeting?') and provide a 1-5 scale 'Scorecard Rubric' for grading the answers.

title: Candidate Rejection Empathy Email
description: Writes a thoughtful, honest yet legally safe rejection email that maintains a warm candidate relationship for future roles.
prompt_text: Draft a rejection email for a candidate who went through 4 rounds of interviews for [insert role]. The reason is 'close but another candidate had slightly more industry-specific experience.' Tone: Grateful for their time, specific about what impressed us (mention a specific thing they said/did during the interview), clear on the 'why' without being legally risky. Close with a genuine invitation to connect on LinkedIn and apply for [insert future role] that might fit their profile better.

title: Strategic Workforce Planner
description: Forecasts the skill gaps a company will face in 2 years based on a product roadmap and suggests L&D pipelines.
prompt_text: Based on the following product roadmap goals for the next 18 months: [insert goals], analyze our current team structure [insert team makeup]. Identify 3 critical skill gaps we will face as a team. For each gap, propose a 'Build, Buy, or Borrow' strategy. 1. Build: Internal training curriculum sketch. 2. Buy: Job description highlights for new hires. 3. Borrow: Fractional/freelance feasibility. Present a 'Transition Matrix' showing how current employees can upskill into these new roles.

title: Onboarding 30-60-90 Day Plan Creator
description: Designs a hyper-specific 90-day success plan for a new hire, including micro-wins to build psychological safety.
prompt_text: Create a 'First 90 Days' checklist for a newly hired [insert role]. Month 1: Focus on Learning & Connection (list specific 1-on-1 stakeholders to meet, processes to read, 'quick win' task to ship in week 2). Month 2: Focus on Contribution (propose a small process fix, take ownership of a recurring task). Month 3: Focus on Strategy (present findings on a 'mystery' problem, draft a mini-roadmap). Include a 'Culture Assimilation' section with 5 unwritten rules of the company.

title: Cognitive Walkthrough Usability Audit
description: Simulates a user's mental model step-by-step to identify friction points in a specific user flow.
prompt_text: Perform a cognitive walkthrough on the following user flow: [insert flow, e.g., 'Signing up for a newsletter on a mobile app']. Step through the interface action by action. For each interaction, answer: 1. Will the user see that this action is available? 2. Will they connect the action to their goal? 3. Will they understand the feedback? Highlight 3 'expectation violations' where the system's behavior diverges from the user's mental model. Suggest UX copy fixes.

title: Mobile-First Wireframe ASCII Artist
description: Generates a mobile screen ASCII wireframe and the corresponding React Native code structure for the component.
prompt_text: Design a low-fidelity mobile wireframe for a [insert feature, e.g., 'Daily Habit Tracker'] screen. Draw it using ASCII art inside the code block. The screen must include: A header with profile avatar, a progress ring, a dynamic list of 3 habits with checkmark toggles, and a floating action button. Below the ASCII art, provide the React Native component structure (JSX) with proper styling suggestions (flexbox directions) but hardcoded placeholder data.

title: Dark Pattern Detector & Ethicist
description: Audits a user interface description for manipulative design patterns and proposes ethical alternatives.
prompt_text: Audit the following interface design for [insert product] for dark patterns. Specifically look for: Roach Motel (hard to cancel), Sneak into Basket, Confirmshaming, Disguised Ads, Friend Spam, and Forced Continuity. Present the findings in a table: 'Pattern Found,' 'Location/Description,' 'Ethical Threat Level (High/Medium/Low),' and 'Ethical Alternative Design.' The alternative must still consider business metrics but respect user autonomy. Description: [describe the flow]

title: Design Token Taxonomy Architect
description: Creates a tiered semantic design token system (primitive, semantic, component) for a scalable brand UI.
prompt_text: Generate a design token naming structure (like Tailwind but custom) for a brand called [insert brand name] that sells [insert niche]. Generate JSON structure for: 1. Primitive Tokens: Global scales (Colors: Blue0-Blue9, Spacing: space-4, space-8). 2. Semantic Tokens: Purpose-driven (color-bg-danger, color-text-link). 3. Component Tokens: Specific to one element (button-primary-bg-hover). The color palette must evoke [insert emotion, e.g., 'calm trust'].

title: Micro-Interaction Spec Writer
description: Writes a detailed motion specification for a button or loader, including easing curves and sprite sheet logic.
prompt_text: Write a motion spec for a 'Confirm Order' button on an e-commerce checkout page. States: Default, On-Press (scale down), Processing (loader transition), Success, and Error. For each state, specify: duration (ms), easing curve (cubic-bezier), scale/opacity values, and the exact CSS/GSAP code logic. The success state should morph the button shape into a circle with a checkmark. Describe the 'magic moment' feeling the animation should convey.

title: HEAT Framework Response Crafter
description: Generates a customer support email using the Hear, Empathize, Apologize, Take-action formula for escalated complaints.
prompt_text: Draft an email response to an escalated customer complaint using the H.E.A.T framework. Customer Issue: [insert angry customer complaint]. 1. Hear: I understand you are saying [paraphrase the core issue]. 2. Empathize: I realize this must have been [insert specific negative emotion]. 3. Apologize: I am truly sorry for [acknowledge specific failure point]. 4. Take Action: Here is exactly what I am doing right now to fix it [insert specific solution steps]. Maintain a human, not robotic, tone.

title: Live Chat Decision Tree Logic
description: Writes a sophisticated AI chatbot script with decision-tree logic for handling complex troubleshooting queries.
prompt_text: Write a decision tree script for a support chatbot handling [insert product issue, e.g., 'Wi-Fi connectivity issues']. Start with a greeting and open-ended question. Branching logic: If 'Router is off' -> provide steps. If 'Connected but no internet' -> branch again into ISP issues vs Device issues. Include 'Dead End Escalation' paths where the bot admits defeat, summarizes the steps tried for the human agent, and sets accurate expectations for response time. Output as nested bullet points.

title: Churn Pre-Save Playbook
description: Generates a cancellation deflection strategy based on the psychological 'Peak-End Rule' and offering customized value.
prompt_text: A customer wants to cancel their subscription to [insert SaaS product]. Their primary reason is [insert reason, e.g., 'too expensive' or 'not using it enough']. Create a 'Save Playbook' for the support agent. 1. Opening validation script. 2. Discovery Question: Ask 'What was the one thing you signed up to achieve that hasn't happened yet?' 3. The Strategy: Match their specific pain point to a hidden feature, or offer a 'Pause Plan' instead of canceling. 4. 'Positive Exit' macro if they insist.

title: NPS Detractor Deep-Dive Interview
description: Generates an open-ended survey script to get qualitative gold from detractors without biasing their answers.
prompt_text: Create a follow-up email script for a customer who gave us a Detractor score (0-6) on an NPS survey. The goal is not to upsell, but to understand systemic failures. The email should include 3 open-ended questions: 1. 'What specific incident prompted this score?' 2. 'If you could wave a magic wand and fix one thing about [product], what would it be?' 3. 'Is it okay if a product manager reaches out to listen?' The tone must be humble and investigative.

title: Macro Knowledge Base Article
description: Writes a hybrid help doc that seamlessly blends beginner steps with an expandable 'advanced power-user' section.
prompt_text: Write a Knowledge Base article for [insert feature]. Target audience: Tiered. Structure: Title (Action + Outcome). Section 1: 'Quick Start (60 Seconds)' - 3 steps to success. Section 2: 'Step-by-Step Visual Walkthrough' - detailed with placeholders for GIFs. Section 3: 'Power User Corner' - hidden complex workflows, API workarounds, or keyboard shortcuts. Add a 'Common Pitfalls' callout box at the end with 2 specific error messages and their fixes.

title: Periodization Strength Mesocycle Planner
description: Designs a 4-week block of strength training manipulating volume, intensity, and exercise variation for a specific goal.
prompt_text: Act as a certified strength coach. Create a 4-week 'Hypertrophy-Strength' mesocycle plan for [insert experience level, e.g., 'intermediate'] lifter. Goal: [insert goal, e.g., 'increase squat 1RM']. Week 1: Accumulation (high volume, low intensity). Week 2: Intensification (moderate volume, heavy weight). Week 3: Overreaching (peak weight). Week 4: Deload. For each training day, list exercises, rep schemes, RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion), and rest periods. Provide RIR (Reps in Reserve) targets.

title: Bio-Individual Nutrition Elimination Diet
description: Creates a 21-day low-inflammation meal plan protocol with a systematic reintroduction phase to find food sensitivities.
prompt_text: Design a 21-day Autoimmune Protocol (AIP) style elimination diet meal plan. Dietary preferences: [insert, e.g., 'no seafood', 'dairy-free']. Week 1-3: Remove grains, legumes, nightshades, eggs, dairy, nuts/seeds. Provide a daily meal plan (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) with macronutrient balance focus. Critical: After the 21 days, provide a 'Reintroduction Schedule' where the user adds back one food group every 3 days and tracks symptoms (bloating, brain fog, skin). Include a food journal template.

title: Zone 2 Cardio Optimization Protocol
description: Explains the science of mitochondrial efficiency and provides a personalized Zone 2 heart rate training schedule.
prompt_text: Explain the concept of Zone 2 cardio training to a [insert fitness level] runner. Calculate my estimated Zone 2 heart rate range using the 'Maffetone Formula' (180 - Age) and the 'Talk Test' method. Create a 6-week steady-state cardio plan focusing strictly on staying in this zone. Include 2 sessions per week, increasing by 10 minutes every 2 weeks. Address the 'dreaded plateau' and explain why going faster in these sessions ruins the adaptation goal.

title: Sleep Hygiene Stimulus Control Plan
description: Generates a CBT-I inspired protocol to cure behavioral insomnia through stimulus control and sleep restriction.
prompt_text: Act as a sleep psychologist. I have issues with [insert issue, e.g., 'lying in bed for hours unable to fall asleep']. Design a 2-week Stimulus Control protocol. Rules: 1. 'The 20-Minute Rule': If not asleep in 20 minutes, get up and do a boring task in dim light (list 5 tasks). 2. Bed/Sleep Resynchronization: prescribed sleep window calculation based on my wake time. 3. Wind-Down Routine: Hour-by-hour schedule starting 3 hours before bed.

title: Mental Health Daily CBT Journal
description: Provides a structured daily Cognitive Behavioral Therapy thought record journal to challenge negative automatic thoughts.
prompt_text: Generate a 7-day CBT Thought Record template. The daily entry must include these columns: 1. Situation/Trigger (Objective fact). 2. Automatic Thought (Percentage belief 0-100). 3. Cognitive Distortion Identified (e.g., Catastrophizing, Mind Reading). 4. Evidence For vs. Evidence Against. 5. Balanced Alternative Thought. 6. Rerate Belief (0-100). Also, include a daily 'Behavioral Activation' block: one small action to break the rumination cycle.

title: Multi-Sensory Listing Description
description: Writes a real estate listing that skips the floorplan listing and focuses on the 'feeling' and lifestyle of each room.
prompt_text: Write a luxury real estate listing description for [insert property type, e.g., 'a mid-century modern hillside home']. Do NOT just list features. Sensory-immerse the reader: Morning light spilling through floor-to-ceiling glass, the sound of a water feature by the entrance, the warmth of walnut floors underfoot. Describe the 'Sunday morning routine' living there. Include a 'Chef's Kitchen' paragraph and a 'Master Suite Sanctuary' paragraph. SEO Keywords to blend: [insert local keywords].

title: Seller Objection Pricing Script
description: Generates a script for realtors to justify a listing price using absorption rate data and overcoming emotional attachment.
prompt_text: Act as a listing agent coach. I have a seller who insists on pricing their home [insert X% above market comps]. Generate a dialogue script to handle this objection. Use the 'Feel-Felt-Found' method on the emotional side. Then, bring hard data: explain the 'Absorption Rate' and 'Days on Market' penalty for overpricing. Include the 'Price Reduction Stigma' argument. Close with a compromise strategy: 'The 30-day conditional test at the market price.'

title: Hyper-Local Community Guide Content
description: Creates a 'neighborhood spotlight' blog post to attract organic traffic from families researching local schools and parks.
prompt_text: Write a 'Neighborhood Spotlight' SEO blog post about [insert neighborhood/city]. Target audience: Young families moving to the area. Outline: 1. Vibe (Hip, Quiet, Up-and-coming?). 2. School District Rankings (mention top 3 schools). 3. Hidden Gems (coffee shops, parks, the butcher that gives cookies to kids). 4. Commute Times (to main business districts). 5. Housing Stock (types of architecture). Tone: Knowledgeable local friend. Include a map embed placeholder and 'Newest Listings' widget note.

title: Facebook Lead Gen Real Estate Funnel
description: Designs the copy and image strategy for a 'Homes Under Market Value' Facebook Lead Form campaign.
prompt_text: Create a Facebook Lead Gen campaign for [insert farm area] targeting first-time homebuyers. Headline: 'Homes in [Farm Area] You Can't Find on Zillow.' Primary Text: Focus on the fear of missing out on off-market deals. Provide the exact questions to put on the Lead Form (keep it 4 questions max to maximize conversion). Suggest image creative: a split screen of 'Sold' signs vs a family in front of a home. Compliance note: standard Equal Housing disclaimer.

title: CMA (Comparative Market Analysis) Narrator
description: Translates a dry excel sheet of comps into a conversational narrative report for a seller client.
prompt_text: Turn the following raw data about comps into a CMA narrative report for my seller. Data: [paste comp data, e.g., Address, SqFt, Sold Price, DOM]. Write a 4-paragraph summary: 1. Executive Summary: price per square foot range. 2. The 'Winner' Comp: the highest sale and why it supports our price. 3. The 'Dog' Comp: the lowest sale and why ours is superior. 4. Recommended Listing Strategy: Price band suggestion and the 'psychological pricing' reasoning (e.g., $499k vs $505k).

title: Character Diamond Interview
description: Puts a fictional character through a deep psychological interview to uncover their ghost, flaw, want, and need.
prompt_text: Interview my fictional character named [insert name]. Ask them 10 deep questions one by one to build a 'Character Diamond.' Dig for: 1. The Core Lie they believe about the world. 2. The Ghost (past trauma that formed the lie). 3. The Want (external goal). 4. The Need (internal truth). 5. The Point of No Return. Ask me these questions sequentially in first-person POV as if you are a therapist talking to the character. Do not list them all at once.

title: Save the Cat! Beat Sheet Mapper
description: Outlines a full novel or screenplay using the 15-beat Blake Snyder structure tailored to a specific genre.
prompt_text: Act as a story development editor. Outline a [insert genre, e.g., 'Sci-Fi Thriller'] screenplay/novel using the Save the Cat! 15-beat structure. The logline is: [insert logline]. Map out the beats: 1. Opening Image, 2. Theme Stated, 3. Set-Up, 4. Catalyst, 5. Debate... through 15. Final Image. For each beat, specify the page number range (if 110-page script) and write a 2-sentence description of exactly what visually happens and the emotional shift.

title: Subtext-Rich Dialogue Polisher
description: Rewrites 'on-the-nose' dialogue to include conflict, hidden agendas, and iceberg theory subtext.
prompt_text: The following dialogue is too 'on the nose' (characters say exactly what they mean). Rewrite it so the subtext does the work. Dialogue: [insert clunky dialogue]. Rules: 1. No character can directly state their emotional need. 2. Add an 'action car' (physical business) that contrasts the words. 3. Use the 'Lateral Move' technique: answer questions with unrelated questions to show discomfort. 4. End with a 'loaded silence' beat description.

title: Worldbuilding Societal Pillars
description: Creates a functional fictional world by defining its economy, belief system, government, and technology in conflict.
prompt_text: Build the foundational 'Four Pillars' for my fantasy/sci-fi world. 1. Economics: What is the resource that controls power (spice/gold/data)? 2. Belief: What religion/cult/philosophy is dominant, and who is the heretic? 3. Government: Describe the bureaucracy or monarchy structure and its critical flaw. 4. Technology/Magic: Define the hard limits of the magic/tech system (Sanderson's Law). Most importantly, describe how these 4 pillars directly clash with each other to create central conflict.

title: Synesthesia-Inspired Descriptive Prose
description: Transforms a bland scene description into a synesthetic experience, mixing senses to achieve a distinct voice.
prompt_text: Rewrite the following bland scene description using synesthesia and advanced sensory cross-wiring. Scene: [insert scene, e.g., 'walking through a busy market']. Replace visual-only descriptors with mixed senses: e.g., 'the sound of heat,' 'the taste of bright yellow,' 'the smell of dust heavy with stories.' Aim for a style reminiscent of [insert author style reference, e.g., Ray Bradbury or Gabriel Garcia Marquez]. Use onomatopoeia and internal rhythm.

title: Podcast Intro Hook Clinic
description: Analyzes a cold open for a podcast and rewrites it using 3 proven narrative structures to maximize listen-through rate.
prompt_text: Analyze the following podcast cold open script. Identify the 'moment of tension' or 'promise.' If it's absent, suggest a clip that creates it. Provide 3 re-cut versions of the intro: 1. The 'Flash-Forward' (start at the most dramatic point, then cut to the introduction). 2. The 'Rhetorical Question' (start with a provocative question). 3. The 'Scene-Setting' (cinematic audio description). Script: [paste current intro script]

title: Guest Research Deep-Dive Brief
description: Compiles a structured prep document for an interview, uncovering the guest's contrarian opinion to spark debate.
prompt_text: Create a 'Guest Interview Prep' document for [insert guest name and credentials]. Based on their public content, identify: 1. The 'Surface Take' (what they always talk about). 2. The 'Contrarian Spark' (an opinion they hold that the public disagrees with). 3. The 'Emotional Origin' (childhood/early career story that shaped them). 4. 'Lightning Round' Questions (3 weird specific questions). Goal: Elevate the interview from a boring bio-read to a real conversation.

title: Multilingual Episode Show Notes
description: Generates detailed SEO-optimized show notes with timestamps, bulleted takeaways, and bilingual vocabulary blocks.
prompt_text: Write the show notes for a podcast episode about [insert topic]. Format: 1. SEO Title (under 60 chars). 2. Episode Summary (3 sentences with emotional hook). 3. Timestamps (5 major time blocks with catchy labels, not just generic segments). 4. Key Takeaways (5-7 bullet points of actionable wisdom). 5. Resources/Links Mentioned. 6. [Insert Language] Vocabulary Corner: define 3 advanced jargon terms used in the episode.

title: Sonic Branding & Sound Design Brief
description: Writes a creative brief for an audio engineer to design show intro music and transition stings matching a brand vibe.
prompt_text: Write a creative brief for a sound designer to create my podcast's audio branding. Podcast vibe: [insert, e.g., 'True crime mixed with dark humor']. Describe the 'Audio Logo' (3-second sonic signature): Instruments (e.g., 'distorted cello and a vintage typewriter ding'), Tempo, and Emotional Color. Describe 'Transition Stings' (for suspense/big reveals). Describe 'Background Ambient Texture.' Provide 3 reference tracks or movie scores for inspiration.

title: Solo Episode Narrative Arc
description: Structures a scripted solo podcast episode around the Hero’s Journey to stop the rambling and hold attention.
prompt_text: Structure a 20-minute solo podcast episode on [insert personal story or lesson]. Use Joseph Campbell's Hero's Journey framework in a micro-format. 1. Ordinary World (setup). 2. Call to Adventure (inciting incident). 3. Refusal of the Call (internal resistance). 4. Meeting the Mentor (book/person/quote). 5. The Ordeal (the crisis/climax). 6. The Return with the Elixir (the lesson for the listener). Write the voiceover script for the 'Ordeal' section in high detail.

title: Hybrid Event Run of Show (ROS)
description: Generates a minute-by-minute technical run of show coordinating virtual speakers, physical venue cues, and streaming.
prompt_text: Create a detailed Run of Show for a hybrid conference for [insert audience]. Total duration: [X] hours. Include columns: Timecode, Duration, Session Name, In-Room Activity, Virtual Platform Activity (Zoom/Hopin), Speaker Name, AV Cue (Slides/Video), and Backstage Notes. The opening must include a 'Virtual Handshake' networking icebreaker. Add pre-recorded backup video triggers in case of live stream lag. Format as a Markdown table.

title: Event Sponsorship Tier Architect
description: Designs high-value, sellable sponsorship packages with creative non-monetary asset swaps for B2B events.
prompt_text: Design 3 tiers of sponsorship packages for a [insert event type, e.g., 'Tech Startups Happy Hour']. Tier 1: 'Partner' (Cash $5k + Value-in-kind). Tier 2: 'Exhibitor' ($2k). Tier 3: 'Community Ally' ($500). For each tier, list the Value Proposition, Logos on Assets, Speaking Opportunities, and 'Experiential Activation' (e.g., branded charging station). Include an 'In-Kind Trade Offer' list: venue, AV, beverages, swag. Focus on the ROI metrics we provide post-event.

title: Venue Logistics Risk Register
description: Compiles a comprehensive risk management plan covering weather, technical failure, medical, and security scenarios.
prompt_text: Create an Event Risk Register for an [insert type of outdoor event, e.g., 'outdoor food truck festival'] for 500 attendees. Categorize risks into: Weather (rain/wind/heavy sun), Technical (power outage), Security (lost child protocol/crowd crush), Food Safety, and PR (social media backlash). Provide a standard matrix for: Likelihood (1-5), Severity (1-5), Risk Score. For the top 3 highest scores, write the detailed 'Incident Response Playbook' for the on-the-ground team.

title: Pre-Event Engagement Email Sequence
description: Drafts a 4-email pre-event sequence to reduce no-shows by building hype and setting actionable attendance goals.
prompt_text: Write a 4-part 'Attendee Hype' email sequence for a [insert event name]. Email 1 (Confirmation): 'You're in! Here's your challenge...' (assign them a networking mission). Email 2 (7 days out): Speaker highlight and 'appetizer' content. Email 3 (3 days out): Logistics + Social proof ('See who's attending'). Email 4 (Day before): 'Last Checklist' + Weather/Outfit recommendation + Parking cheat code. Use a countdown timer GIF placeholder in each.

title: Post-Mortem Data Retrospective
description: Guides a structured meeting to analyze post-event survey data and extract actionable improvements for the next iteration.
prompt_text: Lead a 'Post-Mortem Retrospective' for our event team. We have the following NPS score and feedback: [insert data]. Facilitate a 'Start, Stop, Continue' framework. Start: What new ideas came from the feedback? Stop: What processes burned out the staff or didn't impact the attendee? Continue: What golden moments must we keep? Also, analyze the 'registration-to-check-in conversion rate' and brainstorm a 'friction point' heatmap for the attendee journey map.

title: RPG Faction Codex & Diplomacy Matrix
description: Creates a dynamic political matrix between factions, defining their allies, enemies, and forbidden resources.
prompt_text: Create a Faction Codex for my [insert genre, e.g., 'Post-Apocalyptic Wasteland'] RPG game. Generate 4 distinct factions. For each, detail: 1. Sigil & Colors. 2. Core Philosophy (one-liner). 3. The 'Sacred Resource' they hoard. 4. The 'Heresy' that gets you exiled. Then, create a 'Diplomacy Matrix' table (Faction vs Faction): Status (Allied/Neutral/War), Public Perception vs True Intention. Describe a 'Proxy War' zone where they clash indirectly using mercenaries.

title: Side Quest Morality Dilemma Designer
description: Crafts a Witcher-style side quest where there is no 'right' answer, only a choice between two conflicting moral evils.
prompt_text: Design a 'Morally Gray' side quest for an RPG in [insert setting]. The quest hook: [insert hook, e.g., 'A village is mysteriously immune to a plague ravaging the kingdom']. Introduce the 'Two-Pronged Dilemma.' Option A: The 'Merciful' solution has terrible long-term consequences. Option B: The 'Harsh' solution breaks the hero's code but solves it. Write the dialogue tree for the 'climax' where the NPC reveals the twist. Ensure both rewards are materially similar but narratively shocking.

title: Boss Fight Mechanics & Phase Script
description: Designs a multi-phase boss encounter with unique mechanics, environmental hazards, and enrage timers.
prompt_text: Design a 'Dark Souls' style boss encounter named '[Insert Boss Name]'. Visual description and lore intro. Phase 1 Mechanics: Basic attack patterns, tells (wind-up animations), parry windows. Phase 2 Shift (at 50% HP): Environmental change (e.g., arena floods), new 'Fury' combo set. Phase 3 (Enrage at 10% HP): Drastic speed increase, desperation move (one-shot mechanic). Include the 'Victory Death Monologue' text and the unique loot drop with flavor text.

title: Player Dialogue Choice Architecture
description: Writes a branching dialogue tree where choices impact companion affinity and world state, not just the immediate reply.
prompt_text: Write a branching dialogue script for a conversation with an NPC named [insert name] about [insert topic]. Offer the player 4 dialogue choices: 1. 'Paragon' (Selfless). 2. 'Renegade' (Aggressive). 3. 'Intellect' (Investigation). 4. 'Coin' (Bribery/Capitalist). For each choice, show the NPC's immediate reaction AND the hidden variable changes: [Companion A Affinity +2], [Faction B Reputation -5]. Also, show the 'Silent Protagonist' gesture described for cutscene direction.

title: Deep Lore Environmental Storyteller
description: Describes a game level's environment where every asset tells a story, creating archaeological narrative without words.
prompt_text: Describe a game level environment for a [insert game type, e.g., 'survival horror'] game. The setting: [insert location, e.g., 'Abandoned Lunar Research Base']. Apply 'Environmental Storytelling' principles. Describe: 1. The 'Golden Path' lighting leading the player. 2. The 'Vista' reveal moment. 3. 3 specific static props that tell a mini-story of the last 24 hours of the crew (e.g., a knocked-over chess board mid-game, frozen coffee cup, scattered medical syringes). No audio logs or diaries allowed.
